paragraphs: This paper studies how a Vision Transformer transfers knowledge to a new domain when only a few labeled examples are available there. Its starting observation is surprisingly simple: randomly initializing the CLS token, instead of transferring its learned source-domain parameters, consistently improved target-domain performance in the authors' experiments. This identifies one small part of the model as an important influence on transfer.

The authors explain this behavior by finding that the CLS token absorbs information specific to the source domain through the transformer's structure. They connect that domain information to low-frequency components in the Fourier representation of images. The implication is that transferring the token can also transfer domain-specific information that is less useful in the new setting.

Their method therefore separates domain information in the CLS token during source training and adapts the token on the target domain. Experiments on four benchmarks support the explanation and report state-of-the-art performance. The findings make the CLS token a concrete target for improving few-shot adaptation.
neurips-2024-a-closer-look-at-the-cls-to.tldr: Managing domain information in a Vision Transformer's CLS token improves transfer to new domains with few labeled examples.

paragraphs: This paper develops a way to directly control how much a neural network changes distances between inputs. The relevant property, bi-Lipschitzness, places both an upper and a lower bound on that change. In plain language, it constrains excessive expansion as well as excessive compression, giving researchers a more explicit handle on the network's sensitivity.

The challenge is building architectures whose overall bounds are easy to set and theoretically well characterized. The authors propose a framework based on convex neural networks and Legendre-Fenchel duality, a mathematical relationship used in convex analysis. These ingredients support direct, tight control of the constants governing the network's bi-Lipschitz behavior, rather than leaving that behavior difficult to manipulate.

The contribution combines an architectural framework with theoretical analysis and experiments illustrating its desirable properties across applications. Its significance is the ability to make a particular network property an explicit design choice. The abstract presents the experiments as illustrations of broad applicability, without claiming that sensitivity control alone guarantees better performance on every task.
neurips-2024-a-provable-control-of-sensi.tldr: A framework using convex neural networks provides direct, theoretically grounded control over how strongly networks expand or compress input differences.

paragraphs: Open-set domain generalization asks a model to handle two changes at once: unfamiliar data appearances and categories it never saw during training. Recognizing known categories is therefore only part of the task; the model must also judge category novelty. This paper investigates how the order and organization of training domains affect those abilities.

The authors observe that adapting the domain schedule works better than using fixed sequential or random schedules in their setting. Their proposed scheduler, EBiL-HaDS, assesses domain reliability using a follower network. That network learns confidence scores through an evidential approach, with a max rebiasing discrepancy regularizer and bilevel optimization. Together, these components make domain sequencing responsive to learned assessments.

Experiments on PACS, DigitsDG, and OfficeHome show substantial improvements in open-set domain generalization and more discriminative representations for seen and unseen categories. The findings highlight training organization as a useful intervention: deciding how domains enter the learning process can improve transfer alongside the model's ability to distinguish unfamiliar categories.
neurips-2024-advancing-open-set-domain-g.tldr: An adaptive domain scheduler improves recognition and novelty assessment when test data includes unfamiliar domains and categories.

paragraphs: Concept bottleneck models let users change predicted concepts and thereby influence a model's final answer. This paper brings that kind of intervention to pretrained neural networks that were not designed for interpretability. The proposed method requires only a small validation set with concept labels, opening a route to modifying existing models through meaningful concepts.

The authors also define intervenability: a measure of how effectively concept changes influence downstream predictions. They use this definition to guide fine-tuning, making intervention effectiveness an explicit training objective. Evaluations cover synthetic tabular data and natural images, with architectures ranging from fully connected networks to Stable Diffusion.

The reported fine-tuning improves intervention effectiveness and often improves prediction calibration. In chest X-ray classification, the fine-tuned black-box models are more intervenable than the concept bottleneck models tested. The method also remains effective when a vision-language model supplies concept annotations, reducing dependence on human labeling. These findings support adding useful intervention mechanisms to pretrained systems without requiring a concept bottleneck architecture from the outset.
neurips-2024-beyond-concept-bottleneck-m.tldr: Pretrained black-box networks can be fine-tuned to respond more effectively to user interventions on meaningful concepts.

paragraphs: Removing unwanted knowledge from an image generator can interfere with its ability to follow text prompts. This paper addresses that conflict in machine unlearning, where the aim is to suppress targeted content while preserving useful generation behavior. The authors treat unlearning quality and text-image alignment as competing objectives that need to be handled together.

Their framework seeks a model update at each unlearning step that improves both objectives monotonically, meaning progress on one does not require a setback on the other under the framework. They derive a characterization of such an update. They also introduce procedures for diversifying both the data targeted for removal and the data intended to remain, supporting improvements in the unlearning process.

The evaluation reports effective removal of target classes from diffusion-based generators and concepts from Stable Diffusion models. The resulting models maintain close alignment with their original trained states and outperform the tested state-of-the-art baselines. The contribution is a coordinated update strategy for reducing unwanted generation while preserving text-guided behavior.
neurips-2024-boosting-alignment-for-post.tldr: A joint optimization framework improves unlearning and text-image alignment together when removing targeted content from image generators.

paragraphs: Continual learning systems must acquire new tasks while retaining earlier knowledge. Replaying old examples helps reduce forgetting, but the training cost can make these methods difficult to use on resource-limited devices. This paper proposes CLFD, which uses frequency-domain information to improve both the accuracy and training efficiency of rehearsal-based learning.

CLFD changes the input and output of the feature extractor. At the input, a wavelet transform converts images into frequency-domain features and reduces feature-map size. At the output, the method selectively uses features for different classes according to their frequency-domain similarity across tasks. This selection balances sharing useful features against interference between tasks.

Because the framework operates around the feature extractor, it can be integrated with various rehearsal methods. Experiments in cloud and edge environments report consistent improvements in accuracy and training efficiency for the tested state-of-the-art approaches. The authors report accuracy gains of up to 6.83% and a 2.6-fold reduction in training time, illustrating the practical value of changing how replay-based systems represent and use visual information.
neurips-2024-continual-learning-in-the-f.tldr: Frequency-domain input compression and selective feature use improve rehearsal-based continual learning's accuracy and training efficiency.

paragraphs: CultureLLM addresses cultural bias associated with language models trained heavily on English text. Collecting extensive multilingual cultural data can be expensive, and existing approaches may require substantial computation or leave gaps in knowledge about low-resource cultures. The paper explores whether a small amount of cultural survey data can support more effective adaptation.

The method starts with 50 seed samples from the World Value Survey and generates additional training examples intended to preserve their meaning. This semantic augmentation supplies data for fine-tuning both culture-specific models and a unified model, CultureLLM-One. The resulting models cover nine cultures spanning languages with richer and more limited resources.

Across 60 culture-related datasets, the authors report improvements of 8.1% over GPT-3.5 and 9.5% over Gemini Pro, with performance comparable to or better than GPT-4. A human study supports the semantic equivalence of the generated examples. Together, these findings suggest that carefully expanded survey data can provide a cost-effective basis for cultural adaptation in the evaluated settings.
neurips-2024-culturellm-incorporating-cu.tldr: CultureLLM expands a small cultural survey dataset into meaning-preserving examples to fine-tune models for nine cultures.

paragraphs: DeTikZify turns sketches and existing scientific figures into TikZ graphics programs. Its goal is to reduce the effort needed to convert a visual idea into a high-quality figure, or to reconstruct a figure whose original structured representation is unavailable. Producing a graphics program preserves semantic information that is difficult to recover from an image alone.

The authors create three datasets to support this task. DaTikZv2 contains more than 360,000 human-created TikZ graphics; SketchFig pairs hand-drawn sketches with scientific figures; and MetaFig collects scientific figures with metadata. Training combines MetaFig and DaTikZv2 with synthetic sketches generated using what is learned from SketchFig.

The system also uses an inference algorithm based on Monte Carlo tree search to refine candidate outputs iteratively without additional training. Automatic and human evaluations show better TikZ synthesis than the tested Claude 3 and GPT-4V models, with further gains from the search procedure. The contribution combines task-specific training resources with refinement during generation, and the authors release the code, models, and datasets.
neurips-2024-detikzify-synthesizing-grap.tldr: DeTikZify converts scientific figures and sketches into TikZ programs, using task-specific training data and search-based refinement.

paragraphs: DreamCatcher addresses an everyday complication in earbud-based sleep monitoring: the wearer may share a room or bed with another person. Detecting a sleep-related event is then only part of the problem. A useful system must also account for whose activity it is sensing. The paper introduces a public dataset specifically for developing wearer-aware algorithms.

The dataset covers eight sleep events and combines synchronized dual-channel audio with motion measurements. It contains recordings from 12 pairs of participants, or 24 people, totaling 210 hours of recording and 420 person-hours. Fine-grained labels provide a basis for training and evaluating methods that connect sensor signals with sleep events.

The authors test multiple benchmark models on three sleep-event detection tasks. These experiments demonstrate the dataset's usability and the distinctive challenge created by shared sleeping environments. The contribution is a research resource for studying attribution as well as detection, with the broader aim of encouraging efficient wearer-aware sensing of human vocal activity through sensor-equipped earbuds.
neurips-2024-dreamcatcher-a-wearer-aware.tldr: DreamCatcher provides paired audio and motion recordings for developing sleep-event detectors that account for who is wearing the earbuds.

paragraphs: This paper studies how to design a clinical trial when the goal is to identify the set of subgroups that benefit most from treatment. Predetermined subgroups and fixed treatment allocation can use experimental effort inefficiently for that goal. Existing adaptive methods may also focus on finding one best subgroup, even when several perform similarly.

The proposed covariate-adjusted response-adaptive randomization strategy updates subgroup identification and treatment allocation as outcomes accumulate. It also merges subgroups with similar treatment effects, explicitly addressing ties. This makes the trial's allocation decisions responsive to the evidence needed to distinguish the best-performing set.

The theoretical analysis establishes a higher probability of correctly identifying that set than conventional designs within the analyzed setting. It also proves asymptotic normality and semiparametric efficiency for the estimator of the best subgroup's treatment effect, supporting statistical inference as data grows. Validation uses synthetic data from a cirrhosis trial. The contribution connects adaptive experimental allocation with both subgroup selection and statistically grounded effect estimation.
neurips-2024-dynamic-subgroup-identifica.tldr: An adaptive trial design revises treatment allocation and merges similarly responding subgroups to better identify the best-performing set.

paragraphs: Faster Diffusion targets the repeated computation that makes diffusion image generation slow. The authors examine features inside a UNet during inference and find an uneven pattern: encoder features change little across time steps, while decoder features vary substantially. This empirical observation suggests that some encoder computation can be reused.

Their method skips encoder evaluation at selected adjacent steps and supplies previously computed encoder features to the decoder. Reusing those features also allows decoder computations to run in parallel, adding another source of acceleration. A separate prior noise injection technique improves texture detail in the generated images. The approach does not require knowledge distillation.

The authors evaluate text-to-image generation as well as text-to-video, personalized generation, and reference-guided generation. They report sampling acceleration of 41% for Stable Diffusion, 24% for DeepFloyd-IF, and 34% for DiT while maintaining high-quality outputs. The findings show that examining which internal features actually change during generation can reveal practical opportunities to reduce computation without training a distilled replacement.
neurips-2024-faster-diffusion-rethinking.tldr: Reusing slowly changing encoder features and parallelizing decoder computation accelerates diffusion sampling without knowledge distillation.

paragraphs: Federated learning becomes harder when clients have different data distributions. Their training updates can conflict, slowing shared learning, and one common model may not fit every client well. Floco addresses these two problems together by learning a shared region of useful models that also allows local personalization.

The method builds on linear mode connectivity: the existence of linearly connected regions in neural-network parameter space with low loss. The authors call their shared region a solution simplex. Clients receive local subregions based on their gradient signals and jointly train the overall simplex. Each client can adjust its model within the available region to suit its own distribution.

This arrangement gives personalization a shared structure while making global update signals more consistent. Experiments in cross-silo federated learning report faster global training and significantly better local accuracy with minimal computational overhead. The results support learning a connected family of solutions as a way to accommodate client differences while preserving productive collaboration on a global model region.
neurips-2024-federated-learning-over-con.tldr: Floco learns a connected region of models that supports client personalization and speeds global federated training.

paragraphs: Grid cells form periodic representations of physical space, and studies also find related maps of abstract domains such as changing pitch or visual features. This paper proposes a neural-network explanation for that flexibility. Its hypothesis is that the brain extracts compact descriptions of change and passes them to a reusable grid-cell integration mechanism.

The model separates a domain's content from displacement within it, producing low-dimensional velocity estimates that are independent of content. Learning uses a geometric consistency rule: displacements around a closed trajectory should add up to zero. The downstream grid-cell circuit performs this integration during learning, providing a self-supervised constraint on the extracted motion.

The authors report accurate velocity and transition estimates and better performance than the tested dimensionality-reduction and motion-extraction approaches. The model predicts that grid-cell population correlations and manifold structure remain preserved across abstract domains. This is a proposed mechanism and testable prediction about brain function, with potential relevance to transfer learning and data-efficient generalization in machine learning and robotics.
neurips-2024-flexible-mapping-of-abstrac.tldr: A self-supervised model explains how grid cells could map diverse abstract domains by integrating compact, content-independent displacement signals.

paragraphs: System identification estimates the equations governing a system from observed behavior. This paper considers nonlinear dynamics whose unknown parameters enter linearly, a class relevant to robotics and mechanical systems. It analyzes least-squares estimation, which returns a parameter estimate, and set-membership estimation, which returns an uncertainty set containing the true parameters.

The authors provide finite-sample convergence rates for both methods under independent, identically distributed control inputs or control policies with independent, identically distributed random perturbations. These inputs do not actively choose actions to explore uncertain dynamics. Their success in the analysis relies on a key assumption: the functions describing the dynamics must be real-analytic.

That assumption matters because an existing piecewise-affine counterexample shows that non-active exploration can fail in another nonlinear setting. Taken together, the results highlight the importance of the dynamics' differentiability properties when assessing whether passive random excitation is sufficient. Numerical experiments on a pendulum and a quadrotor compare the theoretical bounds with observed estimation performance, connecting the finite-sample analysis to concrete dynamical examples.
neurips-2024-identification-of-analytic-.tldr: Real-analytic dynamics enable finite-sample guarantees for estimating linearly parameterized nonlinear systems using non-active random inputs.

paragraphs: A spectrogram represents sound as a two-dimensional array, but its appearance usually differs sharply from an ordinary image. Conversely, interpreting an ordinary image as a spectrogram tends to produce unnatural audio. This paper asks whether a single generated representation can work in both roles: recognizable imagery when viewed and natural audio when played.

The method combines pretrained text-to-image and text-to-spectrogram diffusion models that share a latent space. During generation, both models denoise the noisy latent representation in parallel. Their combined influence produces a sample that is likely under both models, bringing visual and acoustic requirements into the same generation process. The approach is zero-shot and uses separate prompts for the desired image and sound.

Quantitative evaluations and perceptual studies support the method's ability to satisfy both prompts. The resulting spectrograms take on the requested visual appearance while aligning with the requested audio. The contribution demonstrates that a shared representation can accommodate two perceptual interpretations through cooperation between existing generative models.
neurips-2024-images-that-sound-composing.tldr: Two pretrained diffusion models jointly generate spectrograms that resemble prompted images and produce prompted sounds.

paragraphs: INDICT addresses the difficulty of generating code that is both useful and safe, especially when instructions are complex and potentially malicious. Following a request closely does not by itself resolve that tension. The framework adds an internal dialogue between two critics, one focused on safety and the other on helpfulness.

Each critic examines the task and the generated response, using external information obtained through relevant code snippets and tools such as web search and a code interpreter. Their cooperation supplies guidance during code generation and again during code execution. This places critique both before execution, when problems may be prevented, and afterward, when execution can inform further assessment.

The authors evaluate INDICT on eight tasks, across eight programming languages and five benchmarks, using models with 7 billion to 70 billion parameters. They report stronger safety and helpfulness critiques and a 10% absolute improvement in output-code quality across all evaluated models. The findings support coordinated, tool-informed criticism as a practical way to improve code generation across the tested model sizes.
neurips-2024-indict-code-generation-with.tldr: INDICT improves generated code through cooperating safety and helpfulness critics that provide tool-informed guidance before and after execution.

paragraphs: MagR prepares a trained network for low-precision quantization by reducing unusually large weight values. Such outliers make representing weights with a restricted numerical range more difficult. The paper's central idea is to adjust floating-point weights before quantization so they cluster more closely around zero while preserving the layer's output.

For each linear layer, MagR solves an optimization problem with an infinity-norm regularizer, which targets the largest weight magnitude. An efficient proximal gradient descent algorithm carries out this adjustment. The resulting nonlinear transformation requires no additional post-processing during inference, so the preprocessing adds no inference overhead.

Experiments on the Llama family report state-of-the-art post-training quantization performance. One example achieves a Wikitext2 perplexity of 6.7 for LLaMA2-70B using per-channel INT2 weight quantization. The result illustrates the value of reshaping the weight distribution before reducing precision: the preparation happens ahead of deployment, while the quantized model can run without extra operations introduced by MagR. The contribution combines a simple optimization target with an inference-efficient implementation.
neurips-2024-magr-weight-magnitude-reduc.tldr: MagR reduces weight outliers before quantization, improving low-precision Llama performance without adding inference overhead.

paragraphs: NeuralFluid provides a framework for designing and controlling fluid systems whose solid boundaries move. These problems link fluid motion, object geometry, and control decisions, so a useful learning system must account for their interaction. The paper brings these pieces together through differentiable simulation, allowing the learning process to use gradients through the simulated system.

Its components include a fast Navier-Stokes solver that handles solid-fluid interfaces, a compact differentiable representation of geometry, and an algorithm that jointly optimizes shape and control. Gym-like environments support learning and experimentation. The authors also introduce a benchmark of design, control, and learning tasks in detailed, high-resolution fluid environments that challenge existing differentiable simulators.

The benchmark includes artificial-heart control design, robotic end-effector shape identification, and fluid-gate control. NeuralFluid achieves successful design and learning results that outperform gradient-free solutions on these tasks. The contribution is both an integrated optimization framework and a collection of demanding environments for evaluating how well differentiable simulation supports fluid-system design and control.
neurips-2024-neuralfluid-nueral-fluidic-.tldr: NeuralFluid combines differentiable fluid simulation, shape representation, and control optimization to improve performance on fluid-system benchmark tasks.

paragraphs: LM-Weather investigates whether the sequence knowledge learned by pretrained language models can support meteorological modeling on devices. The challenge is to adapt that knowledge to weather measurements while accommodating substantial differences between devices' data. The paper presents a generic approach for building efficient, customized models from a shared language-model foundation.

A lightweight personalized adapter introduces awareness of weather patterns into the pretrained model. Devices and a server exchange information using low-rank transmission, which the authors describe as enabling communication-efficient global knowledge sharing while maintaining privacy. The design combines local customization with access to information learned across devices.

Experiments on real-world data report large improvements over state-of-the-art results for tasks including forecasting and filling in missing measurements at different scales. Further analyses support transfer of language-derived sequential knowledge, personalization under strong data heterogeneity, and generalization with limited data or out-of-distribution inputs. These findings make pretrained language models a promising foundation for the evaluated meteorological sequence tasks, with lightweight adaptation connecting shared knowledge to local conditions.
neurips-2024-personalized-adapter-for-la.tldr: LM-Weather adapts pretrained language models to device-specific weather sequences through lightweight personalization and efficient knowledge sharing.

paragraphs: PointAD tackles anomaly detection on previously unseen three-dimensional objects when target-object training samples are unavailable. The paper draws on CLIP's generalization capabilities and connects two representations of an object: its three-dimensional points and two-dimensional rendered views. This gives the method a way to reason about defects through both geometry and images.

The framework creates multiple renderings and projects information from those views back into three-dimensional space. Using auxiliary point clouds, it learns text prompts through a hybrid objective involving both point and pixel representations. Their joint optimization aims to capture general anomaly semantics that can transfer to unfamiliar objects, supporting both detection and localization.

Aligning the two-dimensional and three-dimensional representations also allows RGB information to be added in a plug-and-play manner. Experiments report superior zero-shot anomaly detection across diverse unseen objects. The key contribution is the coordinated use of points, rendered pixels, and learned prompts: auxiliary data teaches transferable anomaly patterns even when training examples from the target objects are unavailable.
neurips-2024-pointad-comprehending-3d-an.tldr: PointAD combines point clouds, rendered views, and learned CLIP prompts to detect and localize anomalies on unseen 3D objects.

paragraphs: This paper revisits Prod, an online-learning algorithm originally associated with full-information feedback. In a multi-armed bandit problem, the learner observes feedback only for its chosen action, making learning more difficult. Prod had been conjectured to be fundamentally suboptimal in that setting. The authors show that appropriately designed variants can achieve optimal regret.

The analysis interprets Prod as a first-order approximation to online mirror descent. From that perspective, the authors derive variants with optimal guarantees against adversarial outcomes. They also identify a simple variant that they describe, with qualification, as importance-weighting free. Another result provides best-of-both-worlds guarantees, including logarithmic regret when outcomes follow the stochastic regime.

The algorithms use straightforward arithmetic updates instead of solving the optimization problems common in earlier approaches. Their significance is therefore both theoretical and computational: a seemingly unsuitable algorithm family can support strong bandit guarantees with simple update rules. The results also directly improve the state of the art for incentive-compatible bandits, extending the impact beyond the basic bandit setting.
neurips-2024-productive-bandits-importan.tldr: Simple Prod variants achieve optimal bandit regret, including a qualified importance-weighting-free variant and guarantees for both adversarial and stochastic settings.

paragraphs: This paper studies how a classifier can adapt to changing data during deployment using an unlabeled stream. Its approach first monitors the entropy of predictions, a measure of predictive uncertainty. A statistical detector looks for changes in the distribution of those entropy values, supplying evidence that the incoming data differs from the source setting.

The adaptation mechanism uses that evidence to update the classifier dynamically. Its target is to match the distribution of test-time entropy to the source-domain distribution. This differs from simply pushing all predictions toward lower entropy. The detector combines betting martingales with online learning, while a connection to optimal transport motivates the self-supervised adaptation loss.

Experiments show improved accuracy under distribution shifts and preservation of accuracy and calibration when shifts are absent. The method outperforms leading entropy-minimization approaches across the evaluated scenarios. The findings support treating the original uncertainty distribution as a reference for adaptation, with detected changes guiding model updates rather than assuming that greater confidence always provides the right learning signal.
neurips-2024-protected-test-time-adaptat.tldr: A betting-based shift detector guides test-time adaptation by matching prediction-entropy distributions to those of the source domain.

paragraphs: Look-up tables can accelerate image restoration by replacing computation with stored mappings, but their storage requirements can grow exponentially with convolution-kernel size. TinyLUT addresses this bottleneck so that more capable restoration mappings can fit on edge devices. The paper focuses on making the tables small enough for efficient local access.

Its separable mapping strategy changes storage growth from exponential to linear in kernel size and achieves more than a sevenfold reduction. A dynamic discretization mechanism then decomposes activations and compresses the quantization scale, producing a further 4.48-fold reduction. Together, these techniques reduce TinyLUT's storage to about 4.1% of MuLUT-SDY-X2 and make it suitable for on-chip cache.

On Raspberry 4B, the authors report competitive accuracy with more than fivefold lower inference latency than FSRCNN. They also report state-of-the-art accuracy for super-resolution and denoising. The results connect memory design directly to deployment performance: reducing table size helps retain the speed advantages of look-up-based restoration within the storage constraints of edge hardware.
neurips-2024-tinylut-tiny-look-up-table-.tldr: TinyLUT compresses look-up tables to deliver fast, accurate image restoration within edge-device memory constraints.

paragraphs: Visual AutoRegressive modeling changes the sequence an image generator learns to predict. Instead of advancing through image tokens in raster order, VAR predicts progressively finer resolutions. This coarse-to-fine organization makes each stage a next-scale prediction problem, giving an autoregressive transformer a different way to learn visual structure.

On ImageNet at 256-by-256 resolution, VAR improves the reported autoregressive baseline's FID from 18.65 to 1.73 and inception score from 80.4 to 350.2, with approximately twentyfold faster inference. The authors also empirically find that VAR outperforms the tested Diffusion Transformer in image quality, speed, data efficiency, and scalability.

Larger VAR models exhibit clear power-law scaling relationships, with reported linear correlation coefficients near -0.998. The model additionally demonstrates zero-shot inpainting, outpainting, and editing. These findings suggest that changing the prediction order can give visual autoregressive models both strong generation performance and properties associated with language models: predictable scaling and transfer to tasks without task-specific training. The evidence supports these properties in the reported experiments.
neurips-2024-visual-autoregressive-model.tldr: VAR generates images through next-resolution prediction, achieving strong quality, speed, scaling, and zero-shot task performance in the reported evaluations.

paragraphs: Guidance steers diffusion generation toward a condition, but a common explanation of its effect is mathematically misleading. This paper rigorously shows that guidance does not sample from the intended distribution obtained by reweighting the data distribution with a powered conditional likelihood. It then examines what guidance actually does in two tractable settings.

The analysis considers mixtures of compactly supported distributions and mixtures of Gaussians. In both cases, the authors prove that increasing guidance shifts sampling more heavily toward the boundary of the conditional distribution's support. They also show that, for any nonzero score-estimation error, sufficiently strong guidance causes sampling away from the support.

That second result provides a theoretical explanation for the observed distortion of generations at high guidance levels: stronger steering can amplify the consequences of imperfect score estimates. Synthetic experiments verify the theoretical findings, and the authors discuss practical prescriptions informed by them. The paper's contribution is a detailed account of guidance dynamics in simplified settings that captures behaviors also observed with real-world data.
neurips-2024-what-does-guidance-do-a-fin.tldr: A theoretical analysis shows how strong diffusion guidance shifts samples toward distribution boundaries and, with score error, beyond the support.
